blocks.text: Mastering the Mac Finder for legal work

As a legal transcriptionist, your file structure is your digital office. Finder is the core of this environment. If you struggle to find a file, you lose billable time. Start by customizing your sidebar. Open Finder, go to Settings > Sidebar, and check the boxes for your home folder and recent folders. This keeps your active cases one click away.

Tags are a visual way to mark progress. Right-click a file and select a color tag. You might use red for 'Urgent', yellow for 'Drafting', and green for 'Finalized'. To see all files with a specific tag, click the tag name in the Finder sidebar. This workflow keeps your desktop clean and your priorities clear.

items: Command + N: Open a new Finder window.
Shift + Command + N: Create a new folder for a case.
Spacebar: Quick Look at an audio file or transcript without opening it.
Command + Option + P: Show the path bar to see exactly where your file lives.
Shift + Command + G: Go to a specific folder path instantly.

blocks.text: Finder search can be aggressive. By default, it searches your entire Mac. To search only the current folder, press Command + F while in that folder. Use the criteria bar to filter by file kind or last modified date. This prevents irrelevant results from cluttering your view when you are looking for a specific audio file from last Tuesday.
Keeping your Mac fast for audio processing

Large audio files can slow down your system if your disk is near capacity. Keep at least 15 percent of your startup disk free. If Finder becomes unresponsive, it is often a sign that the system is struggling to index large directories. Regularly empty the trash and move old, completed cases to an external drive or secure cloud storage.
Why Lazur helps with file management

When you are deep in a transcript, moving your hand to the trackpad to navigate folders breaks your focus. With Lazur, you can hold the shortcut and ask 'Where is the Smith case folder?' Lazur will point at the folder on your screen. You can also ask it to open specific directories or search for files while you continue typing. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your mind on the audio.

faq.question: Can I use Finder to batch rename files for cases?
faq.answer: Yes. Select multiple files in Finder, right-click, and choose Rename. You can replace text or add a prefix like the case number to keep everything organized.

faq.question: How do I ensure my files are secure?
faq.answer: Use FileVault to encrypt your drive. In Finder, you can also create encrypted disk images using Disk Utility to store highly sensitive case documents.
